::: {#thm-advanced-parts}
## Manually linked parts

For every real $x$:

(a) []{#advanced-item-a} $x+0=x$;

(b) []{#advanced-item-b} $0+x=x$.
:::

The labels on [part (a)](#advanced-item-a) and [part (b)](#advanced-item-b)
are ordinary manual anchors. They are not automatically numbered theorem-subpart
references and their displayed letters must be maintained by hand.

::: {.proof}
Both identities follow from the additive identity law, so their difference is
zero. This proof deliberately ends in a display.

$$
(x+0)-(0+x)=0.
$$
:::

::: {#alg-toy-update}
## Toy update

1. Start with an artificial scalar $x$.
2. Form $y=x+0$.
3. Return $y$.
:::

The native @alg-toy-update returns the input unchanged.

::: {#exr-toy-update}
## Update exercise

Apply @alg-toy-update to $x=3$.
:::

::: {#sol-toy-update}
## Update solution

The output is $3+0=3$.
:::

Thus @sol-toy-update answers @exr-toy-update.

## Representative display {#sec-long-display}

The next display defines one simple macro inside mathematics and combines
expectation, a linear operator, an inner product, a norm, and a finite sum.

$$
\newcommand{\toyE}{\mathbb{E}}
\begin{aligned}
\toyE\!\left[\left\langle v,\mathcal{L}
  \left(\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\phi(X_i)\right)\right\rangle\right]
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \toyE\!\left[\left\langle\mathcal{L}^{*}v,\phi(X_i)\right\rangle\right],\\
\left\|\toyE\!\left[\mathcal{L}
  \left(\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\phi(X_i)\right)\right]\right\|_{
  \mathsf H}
&\le \|\mathcal{L}\|_{\mathsf H\to\mathsf H}\,
  \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\toyE\!\left[\|\phi(X_i)\|_{\mathsf H}\right].
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-representative-long}

Equation @eq-representative-long is artificial notation for rendering only.
